title: On $1$-limited and $(1,2)$-domination in cubic graphs
summary: A dominating set $D$ of a graph is called $1$-limited if every vertex of $D$ has at most one neighbor outside $D$, while a $(1,2)$-dominating set is a dominating set in which every vertex of the set has at least two neighbors within the set. These two notions coincide on cubic graphs. We prove that the decision problem 1-Limited Dominating Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete even when restricted to $2$-connected planar cubic graphs, thereby completing the known complexity results for $k$-Limited Dominating Set for all fixed positive integers $k$.
